rated_messages.input_message: Imagine this urge as just another backseat passenger that hopped in after seeing other people smoke. You are the driver and you still get to call the shots.
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.
Take one deep breath and see what it feels like to be triggered and choose not to smoke.

If you find yourself thinking: "I can't do this", "I need a cig", or "I'll just have one", make sure you tell yourself "I absolutely CAN do this", "I'm in control". Take control of your negative thoughts!
Even though you are stressed, are you willing to sit with this urge until it passes if will help you break this habit?
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
Just because other people are smoking, doesn't mean you have to. Practice allowing this urge to be present for 5 minutes. When it passes, give yourself credit.

Imagine walking into a social situation in three months' time as a non-smoker. Now hold that picture and imagine you're that person now. Seeing yourself as a non-smoker now can make it much easier to resist!
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
